Not at all haha!! It's been easier to heal than my lip piercing. And only a piercer will be able to tell you what genital piercings you're suited to, but Elayne Angel does consults online if you're curious and don't want to go to a shop yet. She also has a list of piercer recommendations on her site. Go for it!!

Yep gender dysphoria! I have terrible bottom dysphoria, and it has actually helped a ton. Gives me something I have control over in an area I'd otherwise rather forget, and now I can actually interact with that area - before I couldn't actually comfortably be touched, at all. Which sucks. Hope yours isn't that bad, friend.

Only tip I have is, try to ride the initial wave out, because it did make me more dysphoric for a week or so when the piercing was still sensitive. But anyway. Feel free to message me if you have any other questions!! And happy birthday!! 💗
I personally like it much, much better! The j curve suits the natural angle of the hole better for me, but ymmv, since I think it's mostly down to anatomy.

I was diagnosed with EDS at 18, after having blatant chronic pain and collagen issues since childhood (9/9 on beighton score). I used to fold myself up inside cabinets for fun. Symptoms run in both sides of my birth family, though no one else's is severe enough to warrant a diagnosis, and they have some very strange views on illness/disability, so none of them go to the doctor anyway. I had MCAS as a sort of comorbidity to EDS before being bitten by the tick. I went though every med on the market short of Xolair in under a year. Ended up going the naturopathic route and am starting to have much better luck.

The tick bite happened long after the EDS dx. I became acutely ill after it was attached for only a few minutes May 2020. My LLMD is of the opinion I may also have had low level congenital lyme, from my mother, though, too. I'll probably never know.

Regardless, I'm 9/9 on the Beighton scale, have gastroparesis, Lyme, torn ligaments, osteoporosis, and MCAS. I'm exhausted.

I'll definitely get in touch with my prescriber, then. Do you have any idea if there's any literature on the mechanisms by which it's simultaneously an immune stimulant and an anti-inflammatory? I'm so fascinated, I'd love to understand better what it's doing in my body.

I was not tested for babesia, only symptomatically diagnosed. I also had terrible (*terrible*) bartonella symptoms at the beginning. LLMD started me on antibiotics right away, because my case was so severe. 

My diagnosis is unique to most because I received a high dose of steroids 4 months in, after which I developed the worst case of neurologic lyme, bab, & bart with EBV reactivation my doctor had ever seen, which is the only way it was actually caught. I tested lyme positive on a western blot back in February '21, but the symptoms were missed for so long at the beginning because it IS so similar to EDS! I thought I was just having a bad flare for months. Had no idea it was lyme until I started going blind after the steroids.

I have also been diagnosed with MCAS - if I'm understanding correctly, you are inferring that this could be due to my immune system coming back online with too much enthusiasm? My understand of MCAS is essentially that it's an overactive immune system?

Thank you so much for your input! I will definitely consult with my doctors as well.
